newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate down, baht falls late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate down, baht falls late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate fell sharply to a 10.25-11.25 percent range late on Thursday from 12.00-12.25 percent early on higher liquidity after the central bank's recent fund injection, dealers said.
"Liquidity was quite high and rates should ease further tomorrow as most banks have sufficient reserves before the Saturday (reserve requirement) deadline," said a foreign bank dealer.
The Bank of Thailand said it injected about 22 billion baht into the money market on Tuesday and Wednesday to ease tight liquidity.
Foreign exchange dealers said stock market rumours on Thursday afternoon that some Thai brokerage firms faced financial problems from loan defaults triggered moderate dollar buying against the baht.
They said the baht fell sharply to 25.322-25.332 to the dollar near the Thursday close from 25.302-25.307 in the morning and 25.292-25.296 late on Wednesday, dealers said.
"Foreign dealers are quite sensitive to the rumours, whether they are true or not," a foreign bank dealer said.

The Bank of Thailand denied the rumours and said all finance and brokerage firms were in sound positions in honouring any cash withdrawals by clients and none have been put under special supervision by the authorities.

Due to the bourse's rumours, the one-month dollar/baht swap premium also surged to 8.50/9.50 satangs per dollar near the Thursday close from 6.75/7.75 early in the morning and against 8.00/8.70 late on Wednesday, dealers said.
The mid-rate was fixed at 25.31 to the dollar against 24.32 on Wednesday.
